Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus-memory chromatin accessibility time course
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) with a transient signal, then run ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors (FOS, JUN) and H3K27ac at multiple time points after washout. Persistent AP-1-bound enhancers that stay open after the signal ends, and that prime a faster or stronger response to restimulation, would support a memory role.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during priming versus recall
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) FOS or JUN, or a dominant-negative A-FOS, to remove AP-1 either during the initial priming stimulus or only during the memory (washout) phase. If depleting it only during the washout phase erases enhanced re-induction, AP-1 is needed to maintain memory, not just to establish it.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of history-dependent responses
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA/scATAC-seq on naive, primed and re-stimulated cells, and correlate AP-1 motif accessibility with each cell's transcriptional response. Include live reporters of AP-1 activity to link individual cells' stimulation history to their later response and to test whether memory is heritable across divisions.

ideas.title: Optogenetic or synthetic AP-1 pulse-encoding experiments
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 with controlled pulses of different duration, frequency and amplitude, using optogenetic or chemically inducible FOS/JUN. Measure target-gene output and enhancer state after later challenges to determine whether AP-1 dynamics are integrated and stored, and whether the memory is dose- or timing-dependent.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like function and locus-specific causal tests
ideas.description: Use CRISPR deletion or dCas9 perturbation of AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers. Pair this with in vitro nucleosome-binding assays and Hi-C or Micro-C to test whether AP-1 binding opens chromatin, recruits SWI/SNF (BAF) and sustains looping after the signal is gone. Compare the effects with those of non-AP-1 memory mechanisms, such as histone marks or DNA methylation.
